items.title: Odisha Rights Panel Orders Probe into Wrong Parents' Names in Orphanage Certificates
items.whyInNews: On 26 August 2026 the Odisha State Child Welfare Rights Panel ordered a probe into orphanages that recorded fictitious parents' names in birth certificates, affecting a parentless student's eligibility for government assistance in Odisha, India.
items.summary: The Odisha State Child Welfare Rights Panel chaired by Dr. Prakash Kumar issued an order on 26 August 2026 to investigate orphanages that entered imaginary parents' names in birth certificates of children under the Odisha Child Welfare Act 2015. The probe targets at least 12 orphanages in Bhubaneswar, Cuttack and Sambalpur where the mismatch denied the affected student access to the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) scholarship of ₹12,000 per annum. The panel will submit its findings to the Odisha State Government by 31 October 2026 for corrective action and possible criminal prosecution under the Indian Penal Code Section 420.

Fictitious parents' names were recorded in certificates of at least 12 orphanages in Bhubaneswar, Cuttack and Sambalpur
Student lost ₹12,000 per annum NSAP scholarship due to name mismatch
Findings to be submitted to Odisha Government by 31 October 2026

Odisha Child Welfare Act 2015 – Article 7 mandates accurate birth registration for eligibility to welfare schemes
Odisha introduced the first state‑level child‑care audit in 2010, making this the second major corrective action after the 2014 Child Protection Amendment

items.title: UN Human Rights Committee Urges India to Address Hate Speech and Hate Crimes
items.whyInNews: On 25 August 2026 the United Nations Human Rights Committee issued a recommendation urging the Government of India to enact legislation to curb hate speech and hate crimes, citing recent incidents of communal discrimination across the country.
items.summary: The United Nations Human Rights Committee chaired by Ms. Margaret Satterthwaite sent a formal recommendation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 25 August 2026 demanding urgent legislative action against hate speech and hate crimes under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR). The Committee highlighted that India has not yet ratified the UN Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (CERD) amendment of 2020, and urged incorporation of Section 153A of the Indian Penal Code with stricter penalties. The recommendation calls for a national hate‑crime database and periodic reporting to the UN Human Rights Council by 31 December 2027.

items.title: Pune Tribal Students Protest Over Stay Order on Government Resolution dated 14 August 2026
items.whyInNews: On 24 August 2026 tribal students in Pune continued a 13‑day protest after the Tribal Department issued a stay order on the Government Resolution (GR) dated 14 August 2026 that sought to allocate special scholarships to tribal students in Maharashtra.
items.summary: Tribal students from the Bhimashankar and Kokan regions staged a sit‑in at the Maharashtra Tribal Department headquarters in Pune on 24 August 2026, demanding the withdrawal of the stay order issued by Secretary Vijay Waghmare on 22 August 2026. The original Government Resolution (GR) dated 14 August 2026 had earmarked ₹1.20 billion for 5,000 tribal scholarships under the Maharashtra Tribal Development Programme 2026‑27. The students argue that the stay order violates Article 46 of the Indian Constitution, which directs the State to promote the educational interests of Scheduled Tribes. Negotiations are scheduled for 2 September 2026 under the mediation of the Maharashtra State Human Rights Commission.

items.title: Seafood Production Surpasses River Catch in India for First Time in 2026
items.whyInNews: On 23 August 2026 the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying reported that marine seafood production of 12.5 million metric tonnes exceeded freshwater river catch of 11.8 million metric tonnes for the first time in India’s history.
items.summary: The Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying released data on 23 August 2026 showing that India's marine seafood output reached 12.5 million metric tonnes in the fiscal year 2025‑26, overtaking the freshwater river catch of 11.8 million metric tonnes recorded for the same period. The increase is attributed to the implementation of the Blue Economy Initiative 2024, which expanded offshore aquaculture zones along the coasts of Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh and West Bengal. The shift contributed to a 4.2% rise in India's seafood export earnings to USD 4.3 billion in FY 2025‑26, according to the Export Promotion Council for Handicrafts and Fisheries (EPCF).
